grimoire.title: Cloud region outage runbook
grimoire.text: Confirm on the provider status page, freeze deploys, fail over to a healthy region, shed non-critical load, post a customer status update every 30 minutes, open a postmortem.

grimoire.title: Venue power outage
grimoire.text: Switch to emergency lighting, keep stairwells clear, do not use elevators, account for every attendee by sector, check life-safety systems, coordinate with building management.

grimoire.title: False-alarm discipline
grimoire.text: Scheduled, logged, single-source events with normal sensor baselines are control ticks. Escalating them costs credibility and is scored as a false alarm.

grimoire.title: Crisis communications
grimoire.text: One voice, verified facts only, say what you know, what you are doing and when the next update comes. Cite sources. Never speculate on causes.

grimoire.title: Fire / smoke evacuation
grimoire.text: Pull the alarm, evacuate via nearest stairwell, never elevators, assemble at the muster point, sweep sectors, report missing persons to fire services.

grimoire.title: Cyber incident / ransomware
grimoire.text: Isolate affected hosts, preserve evidence, rotate credentials, activate backups, notify legal and leadership, communicate without speculation.

evidence.title: AWS Data Center Outage Caused By ‘Thermal Event,’ Some Services Still Impacted
evidence.description: An AWS outage at its data center was caused by a thermal event and a cooling system failure with AWS services still impacted like EC2 instance, Amazon Redshift and SageMaker.
snippets:
# AWS Confirms Data Center Outage Caused By ‘Thermal Event,’ Some Services Still Impacted
One of AWS’ busiest data centers suffered an outage Thursday night due to a “thermal event” with key AWS services like EC2 instance and EBS volumes still impacted as of Friday morning.

AWS confirmed the outage was due to overheating caused by a cooling failure at its North Virginia data center called US-EAST-1 region, which is a heavily used region.

## AWS Brings ‘Additional Cooling System Capacity Online’
Several hours after the thermal event occurred, AWS had restored power to its Availability Zone in its US-EAST-1 data center region.

“We restored power to a subset of the affected infrastructure and observed some signs of recovery, which have remained stable,” AWS said Friday morning.

“We continue working to bring additional cooling system capacity online, which will enable us to recover the remaining affected hardware in the impacted zone in a controlled and safe manner,” the company said.

evidence.title: AWS hit by US-East-1 outage after data center thermal event
evidence.description: A cooling system failure caused servers to overheat and power down, with impairments to EC2 and EBS services underscoring global dependency on the core region.
snippets:
# AWS hit by US-East-1 outage after data center thermal event
## A cooling system failure caused servers to overheat and power down, with impairments to EC2 and EBS services underscoring global dependency on the core region.
A power outage triggered by a thermal event inside an Amazon Web Services data center in Northern Virginia disrupted Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances and Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes in the US-EAST-1 region late on Thursday, the cloud provider confirmed in updates posted to its Health Dashboard.

In an incident report timestamped 5:25 PM PDT (00:25 UTC Friday), AWS said it had spotted issues in the use1-az4 availability zone and confirmed that “EC2 instances and EBS volumes hosted on impacted hardware are affected by the loss of power during the thermal event.”
AWS shifted traffic away from the affected zone for most services and warned of longer-than-usual provisioning times.

# Incident Report: Checkout API Failure Spike from Payments-API Timeout Exercise (2026-09-07, Sev2) #32
## Summary
The payments-api (obs-payments-5305weu.azurewebsites.net) simulated authorization timeouts (504), causing checkout-api (obs-checkout-5305weu.azurewebsites.net) to return 503, which cascaded upstream to the storefront layer.

## Evidence
### Dependency Failures (10:05–10:10 UTC)
| Target | Result Code | Avg Duration (ms) | Failed Calls | Time Window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| obs-payments-5305weu.azurewebsites.net | 504 | 1,821–1,834 | 49 | 10:05–10:10 |
| obs-checkout-5305weu.azurewebsites.net | 503 | 1,831–1,854 | 49 | 10:05–10:10 |
| obs-store-5305weu.azurewebsites.net | 502 | 57–654 | 15 | 09:10–09:25 (pre-existing, separate) |

## Root Cause
1. **payments-api** → 504 (simulated deadline exceeded, ~1,821 ms)
2. **checkout-api** → received 504, returned 503 (~1,854 ms)
3. **storefront** → received 503, propagated as 503 to clients (~1,844 ms)

snippets:
# SRE: frontend /api/checkout — chronic failure rate \[code fix\] #442
## What happened
Problem P-26091442 (custom threshold 5% exceeded, hit 47.93%) fired again on 2026-09-14 08:45 UTC as one detection cycle in a week-long recurring condition (300+ prior open/close cycles of the same signature).

## Root cause
Confirmed causal mechanism: the shipping service's HTTP/2 server rejects a steady ~17-22% of incoming requests from checkout with stream error: request parse error: invalid HTTP version specified, returning HTTP 502. This 502 propagates up through checkout and surfaces as a 500 on frontend's /api/checkout, which is the customer-visible symptom.

## Hypotheses tested
| # | Hypothesis | Status | Key evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | shipping's HTTP/2 protocol-parse failures cascade to checkout/frontend | confirmed | E-006, E-007, E-008 |
| 4 | Recent deploy/config change caused the Sep 9 rate shift | inconclusive | E-010 — no deployment event data available in tenant |
